en.title: B-Max Zet Tablet
en.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins D, E, B1, B2, B6, and C during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, lowered physical strength during or after illness, growth periods, and in old age; to prevent poor development of bones and teeth and rickets; to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (lower back pain, shoulder stiffness, etc.), angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema, and dermatitis; and for beriberi, eye fatigue, and zinc supply.
en.usage:
Adults aged 19 years and older: take 1 tablet once daily after meals.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
en.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine; hypercalcemia; sarcoidosis; kidney disease; infants under 12 months of age; kidney stones; severe renal failure.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, are breastfeeding, or have any of the following: hyperoxaluria; premature infants, infants; gastrointestinal disorders such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or regional colitis; cardiac or circulatory dysfunction; kidney disorder; hypoproteinemia; diabetes; gout or existing kidney stones; past kidney stones; disorders of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinemia, diabetic hyperlipidemia, or pancreatitis, or conditions requiring careful use of lipid emulsions; elderly people.

Keep strictly to the stated dose and directions.

This medicine may interfere with the detection of glucose in various urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, affecting laboratory test values.

Do not take together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline antibiotics, antacids, or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist before taking together with oral contraceptives containing estrogen. Use caution when taking together with anti-aldosterone agents or triamterene, as this may cause hyperkalemia. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea or black tea while taking this medicine and around the time of taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, redness, loose stools, loss of appetite, abdominal bloating, red spots, asystole (cardiac arrest), reduced central nervous system function, dermatitis, odor in sweat or breath, hair loss, restlessness, gastrointestinal disturbance, indigestion, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure, pulmonary edema, or abdominal discomfort occurs, or if menstruation starts earlier than expected, menstrual flow gradually becomes heavier, bleeding is prolonged, or symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

en.title: Benfotime Tablet
en.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for nervous system disorders caused by vitamin B1 and B6 deficiency.
en.usage:
Adults: take 1 tablet at a time, once daily.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
en.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine; hereditary conditions such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.

Keep strictly to the stated dose and directions.

If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take together with levodopa or 5-fluorouracil (5-FU).

If hives, rash, itching, loss of appetite, abdominal bloating, nausea, vomiting, or loose stools occur, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

en.title: B-Back Q Gold Tablet
en.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins B1, B2, B6, and C during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, and lowered physical strength during or after illness; for neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (lower back pain, shoulder stiffness, etc.), angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema, dermatitis, beriberi, and eye fatigue; and to supply zinc.
en.usage:
Adults and children aged 12 years and older: take 1 tablet, once daily.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
en.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine; infants under 12 months of age; severe renal failure; hereditary conditions such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, are breastfeeding, or have any of the following: premature infants, infants; hyperoxaluria (excess oxalate excreted in the urine); cardiac or circulatory dysfunction; kidney disorder; hypoproteinemia; gout; folic acid deficiency; hypersensitivity or past hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5.

Do not take together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline antibiotics, antacids, or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist before taking together with cardiac glycosides, anti-aldosterone agents, or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea or black tea while taking this medicine and around the time of taking it.

Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine; infants under 12 months of age; hypercalcemia (excess calcium in the blood); sarcoidosis (an inflammatory disease of unknown cause affecting the whole body); kidney disease; kidney stones; severe renal failure.

While taking this medicine, do not take together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline antibiotics, antacids, or levodopa. en.title: Exeramin B Tablet
en.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins B1, B2, B6, C, D, and E during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, lowered physical strength during or after illness, growth periods, and in old age; to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (lower back pain, shoulder stiffness, etc.), angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema, and dermatitis; for beriberi and eye fatigue; to prevent poor development of bones and teeth and rickets; and to supply zinc.
en.usage:
Adults and children aged 12 years and older: take 1 to 2 tablets at a time, once daily after meals.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
en.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine; hypercalcemia (excess calcium in the blood); sarcoidosis (an inflammatory disease of unknown cause affecting the whole body); kidney disease; infants under 12 months of age; kidney stones; severe renal failure.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, are breastfeeding, or have any of the following: hyperoxaluria (excess oxalate excreted in the urine); premature infants, infants; gastrointestinal disorders such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or regional colitis; cardiac or circulatory dysfunction; kidney disorder; hypoproteinemia; gout or existing kidney stones; past kidney stones; hypersensitivity or past allergic reaction to Yellow No. 4 or No. 5.

Keep strictly to the stated dose and directions.

This medicine may turn the urine yellow, affecting laboratory test values, or interfere with the detection of glucose in urine tests. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline antibiotics, antacids, or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist before taking together with cardiac glycosides, oral contraceptives containing estrogen, anti-aldosterone agents, or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea or black tea while taking this medicine and around the time of taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, redness, loose stools, stomatitis, low blood pressure, facial flushing, irregular heartbeat, skin rash, red spots, asystole (cardiac arrest), reduced central nervous system function, dermatitis, odor in sweat or breath, hair loss, restlessness, gastrointestinal disturbance, indigestion, upper abdominal pain, pulmonary edema, menstruation starting earlier than expected, gradually heavier menstrual flow, or prolonged bleeding occurs, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.
